network.overall_strategy: This network prioritizes surface cyanosulfidic chemistry because it is the only experimentally developed arginine-specific branch in the supplied literature: HCN plus acetylene gives acrylonitrile, which gives beta-aminopropionitrile, then a guanidino aldehyde manifold, then the arginine alpha-aminonitrile. The literature boundary is respected by marking the final hydrolysis to free arginine as speculative, since Patel et al. (2015) stop at the aminonitrile. In parallel, the network includes a late-stage ornithine-to-arginine guanidinylation route with cyanamide, also flagged as plausible but unverified for free ornithine. Ten pathways are listed as two full routes plus shorter valid entry routes from accumulated intermediates; disputed direct arginine claims from HCN polymer hydrolysates are not used as positive evidence, and hydrothermal routes are omitted because the supplied literature gives no arginine-specific kinetic pathway there.

molecules.common_name: formal C5 guanidino aldehyde Strecker precursor

reactions.name: Cu(I)-catalyzed coupling of hydrogen cyanide with acetylene

conditions.other: UV-irradiated near-neutral surface stream or pool; locally cyanide-rich cyanosulfidic setting

reactions.mechanism: Copper-mediated C-C bond formation between HCN-derived cyanide and acetylene generates the activated nitrile alkene acrylonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) explicitly use Cu(I)-catalyzed coupling of HCN with acetylene to make acrylonitrile 33 as the entry point to the arginine branch. A surficial UV-fed setting is preferred because the same chemistry is framed as local surface flow chemistry rather than hydrothermal vent chemistry; copper availability is a limitation, so this is best treated as a niche but experimentally grounded route (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Ammonia addition to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Mildly basic aqueous pool or stream; ammonia-rich

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia performs conjugate addition to the activated alkene of acrylonitrile, giving beta-aminopropionitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) report conjugate addition of ammonia to acrylonitrile to give beta-aminopropionitrile 34, the common branch point toward arginine-related chemistry. This is a straightforward Michael-type addition and is one of the better-supported steps in the branch.

reactions.name: Aldehyde-first formation of the guanidino C3 aldehyde adduct

conditions.other: UV irradiation with HS-/H2S as stoichiometric photoreductant; sequential photoreductive nitrile-to-aldehyde conversion followed by cyanamide capture

reactions.mechanism: Net two-step sequence: photoreductive hydrolysis of beta-aminopropionitrile to beta-aminopropionaldehyde, then reaction of the aldehyde-bearing amine with cyanamide to form the guanidino aldehyde adduct.
reactions.reasoning: This reaction is written as a balanced net summary of the experimentally supported aldehyde-first sequence in Patel et al. (2015): 34->36 by H2S/HS--driven photoreduction, then efficient capture of 36 by cyanamide to give 37. Patel et al. report 34->36 at 45% and the combined 34->37 sequence at 77% over two steps. This is the literature-preferred ordering because the aldehyde reacts with cyanamide efficiently, whereas direct guanidinylation of 34 is described as relatively inefficient (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Direct guanidinylation of beta-aminopropionitrile with cyanamide

conditions.other: Near-neutral aqueous pool; cyanamide present with ammonia-derived beta-aminopropionitrile

reactions.mechanism: The primary amine of beta-aminopropionitrile adds to cyanamide and rearranges/tautomerizes to the guanidino nitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) directly convert 34 to the guanidinylated nitrile 35 with cyanamide, but explicitly note that this guanidinylation is relatively inefficient and leaves residual starting material and cyanamide. It is included as an experimentally observed but weaker alternative branch.

reactions.name: Photoreductive hydrolysis of guanidino nitrile to the guanidino C3 aldehyde adduct

conditions.other: UV irradiation in sulfide-rich surface water; speculative nitrile-first continuation

reactions.mechanism: Net reductive hydrolysis of the terminal nitrile to the corresponding aldehyde under HS-/H2S photoredox conditions, releasing ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative. No experiment in the supplied literature directly reports 35->37, but the chemistry is a close analogue of Patel's demonstrated photoreductive nitrile-to-aldehyde conversion 34->36. The balanced net written here captures the same nitrile-to-aldehyde logic after prior guanidinylation. This branch is therefore chemically plausible but untested, and may compete poorly with side reactions or decomposition (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Net one-carbon homologation to the formal C5 guanidino aldehyde precursor

conditions.other: UV-irradiated sulfide-rich pool; formal net representation of the late homologation manifold

reactions.mechanism: HCN adds one carbon to the guanidino aldehyde manifold, and sulfide-driven photoredox chemistry effects the reductive homologation needed to reach a C5 guanidino aldehyde-equivalent Strecker precursor.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) place 37 on a late reductive homologation manifold proceeding through cyanohydrin/thioamide intermediates toward the arginine aminonitrile branch. The free aldehyde N-(4-oxobutyl)guanidine is not isolated there; in this network it is used as a formal node that summarizes the C4->C5 homologation state feeding the final Strecker step. This is therefore a literature-guided net step rather than a directly isolated one, but it follows the reported homologation logic and matches the independent use of the same aldehyde concept as the putative Strecker precursor in computational work (Patel et al., 2015; Cobb et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Strecker conversion to arginine alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: HCN/NH3-rich pool; near-neutral to mildly basic aqueous conditions

reactions.mechanism: The C5 guanidino aldehyde undergoes Strecker chemistry with ammonia and cyanide to give the corresponding alpha-aminonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) tabulate the late 45->46 conversion to the arginine alpha-aminonitrile at 90%. Because their exact isolated precursor is a late homologation intermediate rather than the free aldehyde formalized here, this node is represented as the corresponding Strecker event from the C5 guanidino aldehyde precursor. The chemistry is standard Strecker logic and is the strongest experimentally supported route currently available to an arginine-specific direct precursor (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of arginine alpha-aminonitrile to arginine

conditions.other: Prolonged mild hydrolysis in surface pools or geothermal cycling; strong acid/base avoided

reactions.mechanism: The alpha-aminonitrile hydrates and hydrolyzes to the amino acid carboxylate level, releasing ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative and explicitly the key unverified endgame. The supplied literature does not report hydrolysis of the arginine alpha-aminonitrile to free arginine under defended prebiotic conditions; Patel et al. (2015) stop at the aminonitrile, and the review emphasizes that no complete prebiotic synthesis of free arginine has been demonstrated. Mild hydrolysis of alpha-aminonitriles is chemically reasonable, but harsh acid/base treatment risks guanidino-group degradation to citrulline or ornithine, so this step is included as a necessary but presently unsupported closure (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Guanidinylation of ornithine with cyanamide

conditions.other: Concentrated evaporitic or geothermal pools; cyanamide-rich, slow aqueous guanidinylation expected

reactions.mechanism: The terminal amino group of ornithine adds to cyanamide and rearranges/tautomerizes to the guanidino side chain of arginine.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative but chemically attractive if ornithine is available. Ornithine itself is reported from spark-discharge and hot HCN/NH4CN chemistries, whereas arginine is not (Johnson et al., 2008; Parker et al., 2011; Ruiz-Bermejo et al., 2013). Longo et al. (2020) showed aqueous ornithine-side-chain guanidination in a synthetic protein and argued that cyanamide could serve prebiotically; cyanamide availability is also supported by NH4CN photochemistry (Lohrmann, 1972). Patel et al. (2015) further show that cyanamide can guanidinylate aliphatic amines, albeit inefficiently. Free-ornithine delta-selective guanidinylation by cyanamide in water has not been directly demonstrated, so this route remains plausible but unverified (Longo et al., 2020; Patel et al., 2015; Thoma, 2023).

pathways.name: Full cyanosulfidic aldehyde-first route
pathways.description: Complete surface route from acetylene, HCN, NH3, cyanamide, H2S, and water through the experimentally favored aldehyde-first sequence to the arginine alpha-aminonitrile, followed by speculative hydrolysis to free arginine.

pathways.name: Full cyanosulfidic nitrile-first route
pathways.description: Complete surface route that uses the experimentally observed but less efficient direct guanidinylation of beta-aminopropionitrile before a speculative photoreductive hydrolysis rejoins the common late branch.

pathways.name: Acrylonitrile-entry aldehyde-first route
pathways.description: Entry from accumulated acrylonitrile into the favored aldehyde-first branch.

pathways.name: Acrylonitrile-entry nitrile-first route
pathways.description: Entry from accumulated acrylonitrile into the weaker nitrile-first branch.

pathways.name: Beta-aminopropionitrile-entry aldehyde-first route
pathways.description: Late entry from accumulated beta-aminopropionitrile into the experimentally preferred aldehyde-first manifold.

pathways.name: Beta-aminopropionitrile-entry nitrile-first route
pathways.description: Late entry from accumulated beta-aminopropionitrile into the experimentally weaker but still literature-anchored nitrile-first branch.

pathways.name: Guanidino C3 aldehyde late-stage route
pathways.description: Late-stage pathway from the guanidino C3 aldehyde adduct through homologation, Strecker conversion, and hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Formal C5 guanidino aldehyde Strecker-hydrolysis route
pathways.description: Endgame from the formal C5 guanidino aldehyde precursor to arginine via the alpha-aminonitrile.

pathways.name: Arginine aminonitrile hydrolysis route
pathways.description: Terminal conversion of preformed arginine alpha-aminonitrile to free arginine under mild aqueous conditions.

pathways.name: Ornithine guanidinylation route
pathways.description: Alternative late route in which surface-generated ornithine is directly guanidinylated by cyanamide in concentrated pools.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Best-supported full route in the network. rxn_001-rxn_003 and rxn_007 match the Patel et al. cyanosulfidic arginine-precursor branch reasonably well. The main weakness is rxn_006, which compresses several homologation steps and should explicitly use 2 equivalents of H2S per the balance check. rxn_008 is only a plausible hydrolysis from the arginine aminonitrile to free arginine, not an experimentally demonstrated prebiotic step in the supplied literature, and it should explicitly consume 2 H2O.
suggestions: Expand rxn_006 into the literature-grounded thioamide/cyanohydrin sequence before the Strecker step.
Specify UV, HS-/H2S, phosphate, and Cu(I)/Cu(II) conditions for the cyanosulfidic surface chemistry.
Keep arginine formation flagged as speculative unless rxn_008 is experimentally validated.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically plausible but weaker than the aldehyde-first route. rxn_004 is literature-supported but explicitly inefficient, and rxn_005 is less directly documented in the supplied literature than the 34 -> 37 aldehyde-first sequence. rxn_006 is again a telescoped homologation and needs 2 H2S by the balance check, while rxn_008 remains a speculative hydrolysis and needs 2 H2O.
suggestions: Prefer the aldehyde-first branch if the goal is to stay closest to the strongest experimental support.
Provide a direct citation or split rxn_005 into explicit reduced intermediates if a 35 -> 37 type conversion is intended.
Define photoredox conditions for rxn_005-rxn_006 and validate hydrolysis separately.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: A coherent downstream route once acrylonitrile is available. The acrylonitrile-to-beta-aminopropionitrile and aldehyde-first guanidino-adduct chemistry is well grounded, but the path still depends on the compressed homologation of rxn_006 and the unverified free-arginine hydrolysis of rxn_008.
suggestions: Make rxn_006 explicit with the documented cyanohydrin/thioamide manifold.
Add UV, phosphate, and sulfide conditions to distinguish photoreduction from simple aqueous chemistry.
Treat arginine aminonitrile as the experimentally secure endpoint unless hydrolysis is shown.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This downstream nitrile-first route is possible but less supported than P3 because cyanamide guanidinylation of beta-aminopropionitrile is inefficient and the direct reduction of the guanidino nitrile to the aldehyde adduct is not clearly established as a single literature step. As in the full route, rxn_006 is net and rxn_008 is speculative.
suggestions: Document or separate rxn_005 into experimentally supported substeps.
Quantify expected losses from cyanamide side reactions and incomplete guanidinylation.
Correct rxn_006 and rxn_008 stoichiometry explicitly.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Once beta-aminopropionitrile is granted, the aldehyde-first continuation is reasonably coherent and literature-aware. The weakness is not the early chemistry but the compressed C4-to-C5 homologation in rxn_006 and the unvalidated hydrolysis to free arginine in rxn_008.
suggestions: Insert the named Patel intermediates between mol_011 and mol_013.
Specify that rxn_006 requires 2 H2S and photoreductive conditions.
Test hydrolysis of mol_013 under mild mineral or wet-dry conditions rather than assuming direct aqueous conversion.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This entry route inherits all of the nitrile-first issues: inefficient guanidinylation, uncertain direct reduction of the guanidino nitrile to the aldehyde adduct, compressed homologation, and speculative hydrolysis to arginine.
suggestions: Prefer the aldehyde-first branch unless direct support for rxn_005 is added.
Add the actual intermediate identities and citations around the C3 guanidino manifold.
Separate precursor production from target-release hydrolysis when claiming success.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: A plausible late-stage subroute, but it begins at the least explicit section of the network. rxn_006 is a heavily netted homologation step with corrected stoichiometry of 2 H2S, and free arginine still depends on the unverified hydrolysis in rxn_008.
suggestions: Replace rxn_006 with the specific literature intermediates leading to the Strecker precursor.
State photochemical requirements for the homologation.
Keep mol_013 as the validated endpoint unless direct arginine release is demonstrated.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: If mol_012 is available, the Strecker step to the arginine alpha-aminonitrile is chemically strong and literature-consistent. The route is still not a demonstrated synthesis of free arginine because rxn_008 is speculative and should explicitly use 2 H2O.
suggestions: Anchor mol_012 to explicit experimentally observed upstream intermediates.
Specify hydrolysis conditions and expected side products such as citrulline or ornithine under harsher treatments.
Distinguish experimentally supported aminonitrile formation from hypothesized amino-acid release.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This is the least supported cyanosulfidic endgame. Aminonitrile hydrolysis to amino acids is general chemistry, but for arginine the supplied literature gives no defended prebiotic demonstration, and harsher hydrolysis conditions risk degradation. The balance check also indicates that 2 H2O are required.
suggestions: Write rxn_008 as mol_013 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002.
Test mild hydrolysis, mineral catalysis, or wet-dry cycling rather than assuming simple water is sufficient.
Do not treat this as experimentally validated arginine production without direct analytical evidence.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Chemically plausible as an amidination endgame, but the prebiotic evidence is weak for free ornithine plus cyanamide in water. The main issue is alpha-versus-delta guanidinylation selectivity and the generally slow, catalyst-sensitive nature of cyanamide guanylation of aliphatic amines.
suggestions: Provide conditions or literature support for selective delta-guanidinylation of free ornithine with cyanamide.
Consider adding competitive alpha-guanidinylation and cyanamide side-reaction analysis.
If this is intended as a plausible branch rather than a demonstrated one, keep that label explicit.

evaluation.network_feedback: Network validity is high: the graph is connected, molecule IDs are used consistently, and the RDKit balance check reports 0 unbalanceable reactions. Two reactions should still be rewritten with explicit coefficients: rxn_006 is mol_011 + mol_001 + 2 mol_008 -> mol_012 + mol_002 + 2 mol_009, and rxn_008 is mol_013 + 2 mol_003 -> mol_015 + mol_002. Literature alignment is strong because the network centers the Patel et al. cyanosulfidic arginine-precursor branch, flags the aminonitrile-to-arginine step as speculative, and does not rely on disputed HCN-polymer arginine claims. Chemically, rxn_001-rxn_003 and rxn_007 are the strongest parts of the network. The biggest weaknesses are the heavily netted homologation in rxn_006, the only-plausible hydrolysis in rxn_008, and the unverified free-ornithine guanidinylation in rxn_009. The single Surface environment is broadly compatible with the cited surficial cyanosulfidic setting, but key conditions such as UV, sulfide or HS-, phosphate buffering, and Cu photoredox catalysis should be stated explicitly. Overall, this is a well-constructed, literature-aware precursor network to arginine aminonitrile with plausible endgames to arginine, but it is not yet a validated complete prebiotic synthesis of free arginine.
